insights.summary: L.T. Elevator's first call after its September 2025 BSE SME listing was about merging Ricardo Elevators, a two-year-old Hyderabad direct-to-consumer home-lift brand that wins 50-60 orders a month through Meta ads (₹46 Cr order book, growing 15-20% a month), for a 2-3% equity dilution. L.T. would make and install the lifts; management expects home lifts (paid fully in advance) to reach 50-60% of revenue by FY28 and plans a new plant for ₹300-400 Cr of revenue by March 2027, possibly funded by a preferential issue. Net margins of 13-16% are expected across elevators and car parking.

what_changed.text: Merger with Ricardo Elevators (D2C home lifts) for 2-3% dilution
B2C to reach 50-60% of revenue by FY28
New plant for ₹300-400 Cr revenue, live Dec 2026-Mar 2027
Likely preferential issue to fund a larger capex

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: So, this is a space which is completely new. It is going to grow very significantly, and we felt that it still gives us an early-mover advantage to try and capture this.

analyst_questions.answer: FY25 revenue ~₹5.5 Cr; now 50-60 orders a month (₹10-11 lakh each), 2,000-2,500 enquiries a month, 2% conversion.
B2C could earn ~5 points more than B2B if selling costs stay within 12.5%; Ricardo itself ~8-10% net in FY26.
B2C advances offset slow government payments.
Nibav (Chennai, ~₹350-400 Cr) pioneered D2C home lifts; Ricardo is the second-largest by orders.

red_flags.text: Ricardo relied on outsourced vendors and had delivery and service problems.
Possible equity raise soon after the IPO to fund a bigger plant.
Cash conversion is weak: government projects pay slowly.
Merger terms not final; based on March 2026 numbers.

watch_next: H2 FY26 results (H2 is ~60% of the year)

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Passenger and goods elevators and mechanised multi-level car parking systems (Park Smart), made in Kolkata; now home lifts via Ricardo
business_snapshot.customers: Real-estate developers (incl. Tata Realty, Godrej), government smart-city projects in East and North-East India, and homeowners (B2C)
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26: B2G ~43-44%, B2B the rest; B2C negligible
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: Urban housing and builder floors, smart-city parking projects, D2C digital marketing
